name: CA-16
label: Safe D

key_factors: District partisan lean of D+25 in the San Jose area
Liccardo's $2.2 million cash on hand versus Soulé's $400 raised
Incumbent Sam Liccardo running for re-election with no funded challenger
Prediction markets price the Democratic incumbent near certain
model.rationale: A D+25 seat, a heavily funded incumbent, and a Republican challenger who has raised only $400 leave no realistic path to an upset, and prediction markets price the Democratic incumbent's odds around 96 percent.
model.watch: Only an unforeseen scandal involving Liccardo or a late wave of outside spending for Soulé would put the outcome in any doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 16th District, a San Jose-area seat, leans Democratic by about 25 points, and incumbent Sam Liccardo is seeking re-election with the full advantages of incumbency. He has raised nearly $3.5 million and holds $2.2 million on hand, while Republican Peter Soulé has reported just $400 in contributions and no outside support. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put the Democratic incumbent's chances around 96 percent.

The structural picture leaves little room for suspense. A challenger with essentially no funding cannot contest a district this blue, and Liccardo's cash advantage lets him set the terms of the race. The forecast expects a comfortable Democratic win in the high-20s in margin, with the remaining uncertainty stemming from the absence of polling rather than any sign of a competitive threat.
